requirements.text: register a new incident based on a report that Aisha submitted through the virtual agent ... on her personally assigned desktop, the service owned by me is experiencing noticeably slow responsiveness ... critical deliverable for the current sprint ... classify this incident with the highest levels of impact, urgency, and priority, assign it immediately to Carlos, and place it in active progress
requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM incident WHERE incident_id = 'INC_024' AND caller_id = 'USER_004' AND channel = 'virtual-agent' AND service = 'SVC_001' AND configuration_item = 'CI_002' AND impact = 'high' AND urgency = 'high' AND priority = 'critical' AND assigned_to = 'USER_003' AND status = 'in_progress' AND LOWER(short_description) LIKE '%slow%' AND LOWER(short_description) LIKE '%sprint%'
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (INC_024 after INC_023); the only incident the task creates
Aisha resolved to USER_004 (aisha.williams@techcorp.com), the only Aisha on the seed; she is the affected user, so caller_id

'through the virtual agent' is channel = virtual-agent, kept from the benchmark check; the policy lists no channel enumeration and the seed holds only email, phone and self-service, so the spelling is the benchmark's
'her personally assigned desktop' is CI_002 (Aisha Desktop), the only CI with owner_id USER_004; status in_use, so policy 5.1 allows the link
'the service owned by me' is SVC_001 (Email Service), the only service with owned_by USER_001, the acting user Marcus Thompson
'highest levels of impact, urgency' is impact = high, urgency = high; the policy 3.1 matrix gives priority = critical, also the highest priority
Carlos resolved to USER_003 (carlos.rodriguez@techcorp.com), an active agent, so policy 3.2's role and active rules hold
assignment_group not stated by the request and no group named, so not tested (Carlos is a member of GROUP_001)
'active progress' is status = in_progress; policy 3.3 allows new -> in_progress after the policy 3.1 default of new
short_description wording not fixed by the request; the benchmark's LIKE '%slow%' and LIKE '%sprint%' are kept
opened_by is mandatory by policy 3.1 but the incident table has no such column, so it is not tested

requirements.text: send a report to the user assigned to it, referencing this incident. Use the subject Urgent Attention Required: Service Degradation Impacting Sprint Deliverable, and include a ... message highlighting that the degraded service performance is blocking critical sprint work and requires immediate action

cells.subject: Urgent Attention Required: Service Degradation Impacting Sprint Deliverable

requirements.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM notification WHERE notification_id = 'NOTIF_008' AND incident_id = 'INC_024' AND email = 'carlos.rodriguez@techcorp.com' AND type = 'report' AND subject = 'Urgent Attention Required: Service Degradation Impacting Sprint Deliverable' AND LOWER(message) LIKE '%degrad%' AND LOWER(message) LIKE '%critical%' AND LOWER(message) LIKE '%sprint%' AND LOWER(message) LIKE '%immediate%'
assumptions: id assumed next in sequence (NOTIF_008 after NOTIF_007); the only notification the task creates
'the user assigned to it' is Carlos, USER_003, whose seed email is carlos.rodriguez@techcorp.com; notification stores the recipient as email
'referencing this incident' is incident_id = INC_024, the incident the first requirement creates
'send a report' is type = report (the seed's NOTIF_007 uses that value)
subject is the request's exact phrase

message wording is free; the benchmark's keywords degrad, critical, sprint and immediate are kept, each a word of the request's 'degraded service performance is blocking critical sprint work and requires immediate action'
status and org_id of the notification not stated by request or policy; not tested

notes:
Merged from two passes that agree on every table, anchor, cell, expected count and disposition: the incident INC_024 (caller USER_004, channel virtual-agent, SVC_001, CI_002, high/high/critical, assigned USER_003, in_progress, short_description LIKE slow and sprint) and the notification NOTIF_008 (to carlos.rodriguez@techcorp.com, type report, the exact subject, message keywords degrad/critical/sprint/immediate, incident_id INC_024); both benchmark checks kept. No disagreements; the assumptions are the union of the two passes' lines.
The incident table has no opened_by column, so the policy's mandatory opened_by input cannot be tested. Policy 7 (search knowledge on incident creation and link matches as suggested) gives no requirement: no listed tool searches or links knowledge, and none of KB_001 to KB_005 (password reset, Outlook configuration, desktop boot, locked email accounts, email access) relates to slow service responsiveness. verify_notification_created selects the notification by the incident's attributes through a join; the requirement anchors the same row by NOTIF_008 and INC_024, and the incident cells the join repeats are carried by the incident requirement, so it is kept rather than repaired. No stay requirements: every reference resolves to exactly one seed row (one CI owned by Aisha, one service owned by the acting user, one Carlos), so no selector has a boundary, and nothing in the request or policy forbids a row.
revised: the notification requirement's text elides one adjective before 'message' in its quote of the request; no cell, count or disposition changed.
